rounds.text: TSC India Ltd (TSC) stands underappreciated based on the evidence provided. Its P/E ratio of 16.8 is significantly lower than the sector benchmark of 25.27x, indicating a potential undervaluation [E6]. Additionally, its Price-to-Book ratio of 0.91x against a sector benchmark of 2.17x suggests that TSC may be trading at a discount to its book value [E7], further supporting the notion of underappreciation. The company's ROA (Return on Assets) and ROE (Return on Equity) are also below their respective sector benchmarks, with ROA at 5.29% compared to the sector benchmark of 3.68%, and ROE at 14.42% against a sector benchmark of 6.81%. These figures imply that TSC may be underperforming its peers in terms of asset utilization and profitability [E8] and [E9], which could suggest an opportunity for improvement or mispricing. Despite these negative indicators, the company's compounded profit growth over three years is impressive at 57%, outpacing both the sector median of 22.0% and its own trailing twelve months (TTM) compound profit growth of -19%. This strong historical performance could indicate a potential for future earnings growth [E16] and [E21], which further supports the argument that TSC is currently undervalued. Furthermore, TSC's median return on equity over five years is 24%, and its median return on equity over three years is 25%. These figures are significantly higher than the sector median of 22.0% [E19] and [E20], suggesting that investors may be overlooking the company's strong historical performance in terms of profitability. Lastly, TSC has a good return on equity (ROE) track record over three years at 25.2%, which is above both its own median ROE of 24% and the sector median of 6.81%. This positive indicator suggests that investors may be undervaluing the company due to concerns about current performance [E44]. In conclusion, TSC India Ltd (TSC) appears to be underappreciated based on its strong historical profitability and potential for future growth, despite some negative indicators in terms of asset utilization and short-term profitability. The evidence provided supports a bullish stance on the company's stock value.
